title: Amsterdam Club funerals and history
summary: Nineteen members died in 1965; he lists his friends.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You got back to and kept in touch with the music world.
Yeah, sure, I keep in touch with it.
Have you ever thought of perhaps teaching?

No, no, no, it's beyond me now. I'm too old for that now. Don't you understand? Listen, do you know what I'm saying? Let me tell you this in all sincerity. In the Amsterdam Club, in 1965, 19 of those fellows died. I have played with every one of them in the Amsterdam. I went to 17 funerals, because we were so close. All I could do was pay my last respects to them, was to go to their funerals. And Dr. told me, don't you go to any funerals. But I didn't pay him no mind, because some of those fellows were like brothers.
And to this day, every time one of the fellows in the Club dies, -- somebody called you?
In the Club dies, well, we go there to the funerals, and the president will lead the eulogy from the Amsterdam and respect and all like that.
So that's the way it is. Now, I'll tell you something. We're an organization that was formed in 1900. We were
incorporated in 1905. Since that time, over 200 of the men that were members have died. You see?
Those fellows have died. I checked out those that I had played with that died, that I knew and played with, you see how many it was that passed? Fletcher Henderson is on there, too.
Well, he was before my time.

Before my time. And the organizers are there, too (unintelligible). Those guys that I haven't checked through are before my time. They had passed. Those that I had checked were those I knew personally and had played with.
